2610.12083.title: All Verdicts are Not Equal: Rethinking LLM Judge Reliability
2610.12083.paper_summary: LLM-as-a-Judge is the standard paradigm for NLP evaluation, yet its systemic reliability remains poorly understood despite being widely treated as a deterministic ground truth. We present a comprehensive reliability audit, stresstesting six frontier models across four benchmarks, five prompt formats, two presentation orders, three sampling temperatures, and ten repetitions per condition. Our empirical analysis reveals severe vulnerabilities: verdicts change across identical replications at temperature zero, position-order swaps flip the majority of verdicts on challenging tasks, and the most deterministic judge achieves perfect consistency by trivially repeating incorrect verdicts, agreeing with ground truth only 51% of the time. To formalize these multi-faceted failure modes, we introduce the trustworthy verdict rate (T ), a unified metric capturing the joint probability that an evaluation is reproducible, order-invariant, and accurate. UsingT , we derive a theoretical upper bound on accuracy imposed by position bias and show that reliability is item-specific rather than modellevel. Finally, we demonstrate that shifting from pairwise win-rate to holistic rubric scoring improves trustworthiness more than any single-format prompting intervention, offering an actionable framework for robust NLP evaluation.
2610.12083.paper_summary_zh: LLM-as-a-Judge 是自然語言處理評估的標準範式，但其系統性可靠性仍然不甚了解，儘管它被廣泛視為確定性的真實基準。我們進行了一次全面的可靠性審計，對六個前沿模型在四個基準、五種提示格式、兩種呈現順序、三種取樣溫度以及每種條件下十次重複進行壓力測試。我們的實證分析揭示了嚴重的脆弱性：在零溫度下，相同的重複實驗中判決會改變，位置順序的交換會翻轉在挑戰性任務上的大多數判決，而最具確定性的法官通過簡單重複錯誤的判決來達成完美的一致性，與真實基準一致的僅為 51%。為了形式化這些多面向的失敗模式，我們引入了可信判決率 (T)，這是一個統一的指標，捕捉評估可重現性、順序不變性和準確性的聯合概率。利用 T，我們推導出由位置偏見施加的準確性理論上限，並展示可靠性是項目特定的，而非模型層級的。最後，我們證明從成對勝率轉向整體評分標準能比任何單一格式的提示干預更能提高可信度，提供了一個可行的框架以進行穩健的自然語言處理評估。
